title: Demotion rule for ml_entry
context: ml_entry is the real-money crypto ML entry leg. It lost 8.21 R of the book's 7.68 R this week, and nothing today can move it off real money however it trades. The performance review proposes a rule: it goes to the demo floor once, counted per entry bar since the served model went live, there are at least 20 bars, net R below zero and an 80% lower bound below zero. On the old model that would have fired (24 bars, -10.90 R). Tonight's revert to v1 restarts the count at zero.

options.label: Grant the rule as written (Recommended)
options.description: The count restarts with tonight's v1 revert. Each new model that passes offline on disjoint data gets a fresh count. A demoted leg keeps trading on the demo floor for data.

options.label: Grant it, but at 30 bars
options.description: Same rule, slower to fire: it gives the 14-month-old model more room before it triggers.

options.label: Refuse; judge it in the weekly review
options.description: There is no automatic trigger. The performance review flags it each week and you decide.

title: How long ml_entry may trade real money on the old model
context: Tonight ml_entry was reverted to its first model. That model's training data ends on 2025-09-22, about 14 months ago, and the freshness check warns. The next candidate is Sunday's (11-29) retrain, graded under the new rule that a number measured only on its grading window cannot promote it.

options.label: Until the 11-29 retrain is graded, hard stop at the 12-02 review (Recommended)
options.description: If the retrain passes on disjoint data it replaces v1. If it fails, the 12-02 review brings you keep or demote with v1's live per-bar numbers.

options.label: Until the Q1 rule fires, with no date
options.description: Only the demotion rule (if granted) ends the run.

options.label: Demo floor now until a fresh model passes
options.description: No real-money ML entry until a model trained on recent data clears the rule.

title: The +$249k estimated MGC row in the paper corpus
context: One ib_paper gold-futures row (id 4773) is booked at +$249k. That is an estimate: it was priced 262 points past its target during the August protection failure, not taken from the venue. On its own it turns the paper book's headline from about -$221k to positive; venue-measured paper is -$67.8k over 908 rows.

options.label: Exclude it from every promotion/demotion read, keep it visible and labelled (Recommended)
options.description: The row stays in the journal, shown as ESTIMATED beside the measured figure. No grade or evidence record uses it.

options.label: Keep it in, labelled ESTIMATED
options.description: It stays in the totals with its provenance label. The headline sign stays set by one row.

options.label: Remove it from the corpus entirely
options.description: The row is dropped from every aggregate, including display.

title: Should the ETF leg's first live order wait on the Alpaca stop faults?
context: The index ETF leg goes to real money at full size (your decision; the PR merges tonight). Today Alpaca showed three stop faults: an unprotected USO with a refused re-arm, a QQQ trailing-stop change accepted but never applied, and a mirror close that never reached the journal. The diagnosis lane can run first, or the leg can go now with the naked-position sweep as the backstop.

options.label: Wait for the diagnosis, about 1-2 days (Recommended)
options.description: The first live order goes once the stop and re-arm faults have a named cause and fix. This is surge item 3.

options.label: Go now; the naked sweep is the backstop
options.description: Trade from the first signal. A missing stop is re-armed on the next sweep.

options.label: Go now at reduced size until the fix
options.description: Trade, but smaller until the diagnosis lands, then go to full size.

title: Should the measured markout cost become the grading basis?
context: A measurement over 2,375 fills found that our recorded costs understate the true cost one hour after a fill by about 3.8 basis points per fill (95% range 0.4 to 7.3). On real-money fills alone the result is indeterminate. If it becomes the grading basis, every backtest's net figure falls by that amount, and some marginal legs would fail.

options.label: Report it beside the current net for 2 weeks, then decide (Recommended)
options.description: Every backtest net gets a second, markout-adjusted figure. In 2 weeks we see which decisions it would have changed.

options.label: Make it the grading basis now
options.description: All Stage-0 grades use the higher cost from this week.

options.label: Do not add it
options.description: Keep the current cost stack.

title: Headline the scoreboard on venue-measured P&L?
context: Today the scoreboard sums every priced row, including estimated and unverified ones. That is why the paper book reads positive while its venue-measured rows lose. The proposal is to make venue-measured net P&L the headline, with the estimated and unmeasured parts on their own labelled lines.

options.label: Yes: measured headline, the other parts labelled beside it (Recommended)
options.description: The headline only moves on numbers the venue confirmed. Estimated stays visible but is never folded in.

options.label: Keep the blended headline with a provenance split under it
options.description: The current headline stays and the split is a second line.

title: How often paper trades get a live review
context: Live review now covers every account, paper included. Each review costs plan usage, and this week's capacity buys about 4 lanes. The choice is between reviewing paper packages only when something happens (a new package, a stop threatened, a big move) or on a fixed 4-hourly sweep as well.

options.label: Event-only for paper, real money and prop unchanged (Recommended)
options.description: Paper is reviewed when an event fires. This saves usage for the surge; real-money and prop cadence stays as it is.

options.label: 4-hourly sweep for paper as well
options.description: Every open paper package is reviewed at least every 4 hours. Better coverage, more usage.

options.label: Paper off live review this week
options.description: Only real money and prop are reviewed until the capacity reading improves.

title: Re-plan L-ML-LIVE (ML in live trading loops; was due 11-11)
context: The goal was a handful of ML models changing live decisions, each on its own evidence. Today ML changes 3 of 9 real-money legs. The main one, ml_entry, is losing and has just been reverted, and no served model is in the trainer's registry. This is the second carry-over, so it needs your call.

options.label: Re-scope to 'one ML model on real money passes the new rule on disjoint data', target 12-09 (Recommended)
options.description: Narrower and measurable: the 11-29 retrain or ml_entry_eq_struct is the candidate, and served models get registry entries.

options.label: Keep the scope, new target 12-16
options.description: Same done-condition, three more weeks.

options.label: Close it and fold it into L-ML-MECE
options.description: Stop treating it as a week priority; the per-decision ML plan carries it.

title: Re-plan L-DESK-V1 (desk production-ready; was due 11-04)
context: Desk wakes run, but the desk was throttled to real-money reviews. DESK-14 and DESK-18G have landed and are not yet proven, and DESK-19..26 are blocked as 'later phase'. Your first priority this week is desk capacity plus the daily macro brief (DESK-MACRO-DAILY).

options.label: Re-scope to desk capacity + DESK-MACRO-DAILY in production end to end, target 12-09 (Recommended)
options.description: Done when the macro brief runs daily, the desk wakes on paper as well as real money, and one apply path is observed.

options.label: Keep the original V1 scope, target 12-16
options.description: Include DESK-19..26.

options.label: Close V1 and track the work under L-DESK
options.description: No separate week-priority milestone.

title: Re-plan L-AM-STANDARD (active management on every real-money leg; was due 11-04)
context: Every AM v2 Stage B test has failed, and every earlier AM random control saw the exit time, so old 'beats random' claims are void. Tonight's c7e3-07/08/09 runs are the decisive tighten tests. If they fail, the tighten lever closes and work moves to another action family.

options.label: Target 12-16: decide on c7e3-08/09; if none passes, re-scope to one action family on one leg (Recommended)
options.description: Keeps the milestone alive but makes the next step depend on this week's decisive tests.

options.label: Make it dormant until an AM test passes
options.description: No target; it re-opens on the first valid PASS.

options.label: Close it
options.description: AM stays as research under L-ATM with no week priority.

title: Tier-2 and operator-only fixes: approve as a batch?
context: Four fixes need your OK. (1) The closed-flat alerter crashes, so 0 of 23 violations reached you. (2) An options close leaves its legs open at the venue. (3) The stale-latch cleanup. (4) A bulk cancel of about 390 GitHub Actions runs stuck in 'queued' since as far back as May. Each is a defect fix with its own test; none changes strategy or risk.

options.label: Approve all four (Recommended)
options.description: Each ships with its test and is verified after deploy, and you get one line per fix.

options.label: Approve 1-3; leave the zombie runs
options.description: The runs do not consume runners; they only inflate counts.

options.label: One at a time
options.description: Each comes back to you separately with its diff.

title: Unlogged skill amendments: backfill once, or retire the ritual?
context: 43 skill and brief edits have no entry in the amendments log, and the gap has grown for 4 audits (18 to 43). Either one lane backfills the log once and keeps it, or we retire the log because git history already records every change.

options.label: One backfill pass by the housekeeping lane, then keep it (Recommended)
options.description: About one Sonnet hour. The audit check stays.

options.label: Retire the amendments log
options.description: Git history is the record and the audit stops checking it.

title: The daily email digest routine
context: A daily email digest routine still runs, and its prompt says you are away until 11-22. It needs a target inbox and a decision on whether it should run while you are active.

options.label: Pause it while you are active; re-arm on request (Recommended)
options.description: No digest emails until you say you are away again.

options.label: Keep it daily to the account inbox
options.description: It keeps running; the 'away' wording is updated.

options.label: Delete it
options.description: The routine is removed.
